contracts.exploreCritic: Score all 30 ideas exactly once on novelty, viability, and fit (integers 0–10). Mark every attractive trap with a non-empty one-line reason. Partition all ideas into 3–6 non-empty underlying-mechanism clusters. Rank non-traps by 0.35N + 0.40V + 0.25F; fewer than three non-traps is invalid.
contracts.exploreDeepener: For the selected target, return a 4–8 sentence implementation sketch, one load-bearing risk, the first concrete coder step, and 3–5 child ideas spanning variations, hybrids, or unlocks.
contracts.exploreGenerator: Return exactly six distinct short {text,rationale} ideas. Generate only: do not evaluate, rank, hedge, or repeat the first three obvious answers; include the awkward middle.
contracts.focusCritic: Score both candidates exactly once on novelty, viability, and fit (integers 0–10), then partition both into one or two non-empty comparison groups.
contracts.focusGenerator: Return exactly one candidate for the named discriminator. Do not widen the question. The counterexample lens attacks the leading assumption; the simplify lens removes avoidable mechanism.

frameCatalog.text: Invert the load-bearing assumption and design for the counter-world.
Delete one architectural layer and follow the direct data flow.
Start at the untrusted boundary and make the interior representation inevitable.
Treat the failure budget as the primary design input.
Design from the operator’s day-two recovery experience backward.
Swap the dominant constraint with its opposite and preserve the observable.
Combine two mechanisms that normally live on opposite sides of the seam.
Find the smallest experiment that can falsify the preferred mechanism.
Import a mechanism from a distant product or market with the same incentives.
Make the solution deliberately self-obsoleting after it teaches the system what to automate.
Let the constrained subsystem become the customer and reverse who serves whom.
